comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation reports results through four business segments (Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management, Global Banking, and Global Markets) and All Other, managed by the Management Team with the CEO as the Chief Operating Decision Maker for capital allocation.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC structure their reportable segments based on the nature of financial products and services provided, aligning this structure with the assessment methodology of their respective Chief Operating Decision Makers (CODM). MS explicitly states its segment structure is consistent with the CODM's assessment approach, while BAC identifies its CEO as the CODM who manages the segments and approves capital allocation. Additionally, both firms define remaining unallocated operations in an 'All Other' category (BAC explicitly states 'remaining operations recorded in All Other'; MS implies this through its three-segment structure which excludes other corporate activities typically found in All Other, though MS's specific sentence focuses on the primary alignment).

sentences.text: The Firm structures its segments primarily based upon the nature of the financial products and services provided to customers and its management organization, which is consistent with the approach used by the Firm's chief operating decision maker ("CODM") to assess the Firm's financial performance.

The Corporation reports its results of operations through the following four business segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management, Global Banking and Global Markets, with the remaining operations recorded in All Other.
The Chief Operating Decision Maker of the segments, which is the Corporation's CEO, is the final approver on the amount of capital to allocate to each segment.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citi is organized into five reportable operating segments (Services, Markets, Banking, Wealth, and USPB) managed by the CEO, with remaining operations recorded in All Other.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and C disclose that their segment structures are determined by how the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) manages the company. MS states its segments are based on products/services and management organization, consistent with the CODM's assessment. C explicitly links its five reportable operating segments to how the CEO (the CODM) manages the company, including resource allocation and performance measurement. Both identify the CEO as the CODM.

sentences.text: The Firm structures its segments primarily based upon the nature of the financial products and services provided to customers and its management organization, which is consistent with the approach used by the Firm's chief operating decision maker ("CODM") to assess the Firm's financial performance.

The business segments are determined based on the products and services provided, or the type of customer served, and they reflect the manner in which financial information is evaluated by the Firm's Operating Committee, whose members act collectively as the Firm's CODM.
